content: 1. Estropipate and Ospemifene: These two drugs enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Their co-administration is contraindicated. 2. Estropipate and Anastrozole: Estropipate reduces the effectiveness of anastrozole by pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated as estrogens may diminish the pharmacologic action of anastrozole. Co-administration is not recommended. 3. Estropipate and Antithrombin Alfa/Antithrombin III: Estropipate decreases the effects of these drugs through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Co-administration is contraindicated. 4. Estropipate and Apalutamide: Apalutamide reduces the levels or effects of estropipate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as needed. 5. Estropipate and Argatroban/Bemiparin/Bivalirudin: Estropipate reduces the effects of these anticoagulants through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Co-administration is contraindicated. 6. Estropipate and Carbamazepine: Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Estropipate and Cimetidine/Clarithromycin: These drugs increase the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Estropipate and Dalteparin/Enoxaparin: Estropipate reduces the effects of these anticoagulants through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Estropipate and Enzalutamide: Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Estropipate and Erythromycin (various forms): Erythromycin can either increase or decrease the levels of estropipate depending on its effect on CYP3A4 metabolism or P-glycoprotein transport. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Estropipate and Fexinidazole: Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Estropipate and Fondaparinux: Estropipate reduces the effects of fondaparinux through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Co-administration is contraindicated. 13. Estropipate and Givosiran: Givosiran increases the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Estropipate and Heparin: Estropipate reduces the effects of heparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Estropipate and Idelalisib: Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Estropipate and Ivosidenib: Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Estropipate and Nefazodone: Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Estropipate and Phenindione/Protamine: Estropipate reduces the effects of these drugs through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Estropipate and Quinidine: Quinidine increases the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting P-glycoprotein transport. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Estropipate and Rifabutin/Rifampin: These drugs decrease the levels or effects of estropipate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Estropipate and St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Estropipate and Tucatinib: Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Estropipate and Albiglutide/Exenatide/Liraglutide: Estropipate may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of these antidiabetic drugs by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 24. Estropipate and Amikacin/Gentamicin: These antibiotics may decrease the levels or effects of estropipate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Estropipate and Amiodarone/Atorvastatin: These drugs increase the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting P-glycoprotein transport. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Estropipate and Azithromycin/Clindamycin: These antibiotics may decrease the levels or effects of estropipate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Estropipate and Cortisone/Dexamethasone: These corticosteroids decrease the levels or effects of estropipate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Estropipate and Cyclosporine: Cyclosporine increases the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Estropipate and Grapefruit: Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Estropipate and Metformin: Estropipate reduces the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Estropipate and Fluconazole/Ketoconazole: These antifungal agents increase the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Estropipate and Lamotrigine: Estropipate decreases the levels of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Estropipate and Marijuana: Marijuana increases the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Estropipate and Metronidazole: Metronidazole may decrease the levels or effects of estropipate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when estropipate is co-administered with other medications, particularly those affecting CYP3A4 metabolism or intestinal flora.
